A phone switch itself is neutral; it's just a tool. What matters is *why* communication changed and whether both people are aligned on it. - If the new phone made it easier to text or video call (e.g., better connectivity, data plans), and both are happy with the new rhythm, that's healthy adaptation. - If one person feels neglected because calls stopped but the other doesn't care, * that's* the problem—not the phone switch itself. - If the switch was a symptom of deeper issues (e.g., disinterest, stress), those need addressing, not the device.
